review_notes: I read the complete target file and checked the relevant FiberBundle and Data.Bundle definitions, especially `Pretrivialization`, `Trivialization`, `FiberBundleCore`, `FiberPrebundle`, and their uses in `Mathlib/Topology/VectorBundle`. I considered the many named wrappers (`VectorBundle.continuousLinearEquivAt`, `VectorBundleCore`, `VectorPrebundle`, etc.) but did not report them because they are useful specialisations or preserve distinct API, as the rubric allows. The reported issue is limited to the two independent fiberwise-linearity mixin classes. I could not execute Lean, so the proposed abbreviation/derivation has not been compile-tested; compatibility with existing `where linear :=` construction syntax may need adjustment.

findings.excerpt:
protected class Trivialization.IsLinear [AddCommMonoid F] [Module R F] [∀ x, AddCommMonoid (E x)]
  [∀ x, Module R (E x)] (e : Trivialization F (π F E)) : Prop where
  linear : ∀ b ∈ e.baseSet, IsLinearMap R fun x : E b => (e ⟨b, x⟩).2
findings.problem: `Bundle.Trivialization.IsLinear` is an independent copy of `Bundle.Pretrivialization.IsLinear`: the two classes have the same field and the same assumptions, and a `Trivialization` maps canonically to a `Pretrivialization` via `toPretrivialization`. The only bridge instance, `toPretrivialization.isLinear` at lines 178-180, goes from trivialization linearity to pretrivialization linearity and not back. This forces manual conversions, for example in `linear_trivializationOfMemPretrivializationAtlas`, where a pretrivialization linearity proof is unpacked directly as `{ linear := ... }` to build a trivialization linearity proof. Users also have to choose which of the two class assumptions is available for the same underlying fiberwise-linear map.
findings.proposed_change: Keep a single canonical mixin for the underlying fiberwise-linear partial equivalence. For example, make `Bundle.Trivialization.IsLinear` a protected abbreviation or derived predicate for `e.toPretrivialization.IsLinear R`, or introduce one generic `IsLinear` predicate on the underlying `Pretrivialization` and expose both namespace-qualified names as notation/wrappers. Preserve the existing public lemma and wrapper names (`Trivialization.linear`, `linearEquivAt`, `linearMapAt`, `symmₗ`, `continuousLinearMapAt`, `symmL`, `coordChangeL`, etc.) as projections or compatibility wrappers. If changing the class declaration directly is undesirable, at minimum add a documented coercion/constructor in both directions and use it consistently instead of manually rebuilding `{ linear := ... }`.
findings.benefit: A single source of truth removes duplicated class definitions and proof fields, eliminates the manual bridge at lines 897-899, and prevents downstream code from needing both `e.IsLinear R` and `e.toPretrivialization.IsLinear R` for the same mathematical condition.
